title: Weeds after a wet week
about: Bare soil does not stay bare: something always comes up. The gantry has no gripper and needs none. It looks the bed over with its camera; green that is not where something was planted is a weed. Small ones it presses into the soil with a stamp, where they feed soil life. Big ones, and those too close to a plant, it leaves for your hands.

steps.title: A clean start
steps.why: Whatever grew wild before is pulled, so the count is known.

steps.title: A flush of weeds
steps.why: Twelve come up between the plants, three of them already big. Only the simulation knows this number; the robot has to find them. Look at the overview camera: yellow-green dots on the soil.

steps.title: Robot: look the bed over
steps.why: The tool camera looks straight down from half a metre, so every pixel is a place in the bed. About 27 pictures cover the soil. No trained model: leaf-green by colour, then the plan of the bed says what was planted where.

expect.say: small weeds found, clear of the plants: {v}

steps.title: Robot: press the small ones under
steps.why: The stamp goes to each small weed and presses a centimetre into the soil. It keeps three centimetres away from where any plant reaches.

steps.title: You: pull the rest
steps.why: The notice at the top says how many are yours. Those with seed heads or creeping roots go to the bin, not to the worm box: it does not get hot enough to kill seed.

do.label: The rest is pulled by hand

steps.title: Robot: look again
steps.why: A second look clears the list. On a real bed this look is a routine every few days: weeds are easiest while they are small.

do.label: Confirm: look over the bed again
